Dated this the 10th day of June, 2025 Petitioner is the 4th accused in Crime No.1387 of 2021 registered at the Thrikkakara Police Station for offences punishable under Sections 420, 406, 465,
467, 468 and 120B r/w Section 34 of IPC, now pending as C.C. No.177 of 2024 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kakkanad.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kakkanad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The crime is registered on the allegation that the 1st accused, while working in the Insurance Section of Sunrise Hospital in Kakkanad, misappropriated and transferred huge amounts to the accounts of accused Nos.2 to 4.

The petitioner is seeking to quash Annexure 1 charge sheet and further proceedings against him by contending that, even if the prosecution allegations are accepted in their entirety, the alleged offences will not be attracted.
Learned Counsel for the petitioner contended that the only reason for implicating his client as an accused is the transfer of Rs.6,39,363/- to his account by the 1st accused.
It is submitted that the amount was transferred towards purchase price of a property sold to the 1st accused by the petitioner, as evidenced by Annexure 3 agreement for sale and Annexure 4 sale deed.
4. I heard the learned Public Prosecutor also.

5. In spite of the appealing arguments advanced by the learned Counsel, I am not inclined to interfere since, the High Court cannot conduct a mini trial or conduct microscopic examination of documents for the purpose of exercising the inherent power under Section 528 of BNSS.
At this stage, the proper remedy is for the petitioner to approach the trial court seeking 2025:KER:40654 discharge, since that court is posted with all materials gathered by the prosecution.
The Crl.M.C. is hence closed, without prejudice to the petitioner's right to move for discharge and by directing the court below to pass a reasoned order on the petition for discharge, if filed.

Sd/-
